# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 70 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 70 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_070_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 8, Part 1 — The Great Willow Tree

**70:1** He showed me a great willow tree overshadowing fields and mountains, and all those who had been called by the name of the Lord had come and gathered under the shadow of the willow.

**70:2** And there stood an angel of the Lord, glorious and very tall, with a great sickle, and he was cutting branches from the willow and distributing them to the people who sheltered under the tree. He gave to them small rods about a cubit long.

**70:3** After all had received rods, the angel set aside his sickle, and the tree appeared healthy, just as I had seen it before.

**70:4** I marveled at this within myself and said: "How can this tree be healthy after having so many branches cut from it?" The shepherd said to me: "Do not marvel. The tree will remain healthy after all its branches have been pruned."

**70:5** "But why did some receive green branches, others dry ones? Why were some completely withered and dry, others had cracks, others were green but dried at the tips, others were half-green and half-dry, others more dry than green, others more green than dry, and others had shoots growing out, while still others had shoots with dried tips?"

**70:6** "Explain to me, lord," I said, "what the various kinds of rods mean — for I am bewildered by all of this." He answered me: "Listen and I will explain to you the significance of every rod."

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to formal correspondence and the systematic allegorical structure of Similitude 8.*
